Today the red coats invaded and burned much of the town in order to steal citizens and press gang them into being soldiers in old world wars under a geas. Much of the city is under rubble.

Shaking his head at the damages done, and managing to get a vague picture of the events from people around, Roy once again stands in front of the part of the market that supplies various tools. All prices in silver. All the little coin he has, not counting what Bo had given him with a clear purpose, in gold and copper. "If only..." he says to himself before stopping midway through the road and getting shouted at by people whose path he blocked.

Roy leaves the market and heads to the ruins of the money changer's building.

Roy arrives, and takes a gander at the rubble. Mess. Only slightly sifted through like someone was trying to get something out. Maybe the owner, the coinage that was in there.
He shrugs, sticks his wrench staff in a small pile of kinda stuck together rubble, and ties the cloak he took off to the staff.

And he starts moving the rubble.

Just getting it piece by piece, out of the ruin, onto some pile next to it. Isn't going to get much done today, but gotta start somewhere.
Grimlock sees you do this and ambles over. She thinks it's a nice game of sort-of fetch, and helps you organize the piles.
Thomas pulls out his Dimensional Essence (common)

It is before dawn. The street sweepers, the lamp snuffers the people who walked these streets in the time between times. They are not alone today. Countless homeless sit on the street, covered in dirt and blood. Shock written on all of their faces. But seeing Roy begin to clear the first stones has an effect. Those closest to him, while still dissociated from everything else, found them selves gravitating toward the work. The hope and forward momentum of doing something. The ties that bind a people together in times of tragedy and grief. The bonds that come of sifting through what was in order to make new.

So a reminder for everyone, don't argue with DMs (especially during events), there are often many things going on at any given time, many of which you don't see.  We make mistakes, but so does everyone, and we often have to make many decisions in a snap and don't have time for a full explanation at the time.  Let things settle then discuss it politely if there is a question about how something went.  Last week I was juggling work, 4 scenes, mod chat, and DM chat at the same time, and I defiantly made a few questionable calls.  So don't forget that we have a lot on our plates at every given moment.

Likewise have some trust in us.  If we have events going a certain way, there is likely a payoff in the end.  You'll get stressed by some of it, and so will we, but that doesn't mean its okay to be belligerent or throw a fit and treat us like garbage.  Just stay tuned and have some trust in us and our story.  25% of the game is ours.  Let us have that 25% with trust that we will honor your 75%.

Lastly, re-read the rules.  I have seen people accidentally break many of them.  Pets, which includes familiars, act AFTER your turn, not during.  Held actions have to be declared on your turn as your action, and have to follow held action rules, including using your reaction, can only have a single attack, and I don't even have time to go into held spells.  Take a moment to review the house rules, because there has been many events I have seen the last couple days that is contrary to the rules we have posted.

Thank you for reading this.
